messages:
Maya Bhattacharya: Quick sync — we need to decide ownership split for the ingress proxy that fronts Hosted/Dedicated/Private and how telemetry handoff should look. TL;DR: we must avoid duplicate metrics and preserve tenant identity across mode switches.
Oliver Chen: +1. do we mean separate proxy binaries per hosting mode or one proxy with mode flags? :thinking:
Samir Patel: Two main options:
- option A: thin unified proxy that surfaces a normalized API and delegates routing to a mode-specific adapter (single binary, mode plugins)
- option B: explicit per-mode proxies (hosted-proxy, dedicated-proxy, private-proxy) with shared lib for common logic
Each has tradeoffs (ops complexity vs isolation).
Jen Li: telemetry questions: how do we avoid double-counting when requests pass through both unified proxy + adapter? also needs to preserve trace/span context across handoffs (W3C traceparent).
Maya Bhattacharya: Exactly. We also need to consider data residency for Private — telemetry may need to stay local or be scrubbed.
Oliver Chen: Ops perspective: per-mode proxies let us apply different routing/circuit-breakers per product tier without runtime flags. But releases multiply.
Samir Patel: Unified proxy simplifies rollout and client trust boundary, but mode adapters add escape hatches when a private deployment wants strict egress rules.
Dana Morris: Compliance note — Private customers may require that no identifiers leave their VPC. So telemetry schema must support redaction or in-place aggregation.
Jen Li: Proposal for telemetry handoff: emit a single canonical event at proxy exit with fields: `mode`, `tenant_id_hash`, `route`, `latency_ms`, `sampled_trace` (bool). Avoid sending raw tenant IDs.
Samir Patel: Implementation sketch: adapters must call `handoff.emit(event)` which will either forward to central telemetry or write to local sink depending on `mode`. Simple API: `handoff.emit({k:v})` — adapter decides sink.
Maya Bhattacharya: Example config snippet for hosted vs private (idea):
```
proxy:
  mode: hosted # hosted|dedicated|private
  telemetry:
    sink: central|local
    sample_rate: 0.05
    redaction: tenant_hash
```
Oliver Chen: Question: how do we handle fallbacks? If hosted capacity is saturated and we route to dedicated, do we preserve the same tenant identifier semantics? We must guarantee stable `tenant_id_hash` across routing.
Jen Li: Yes — tenant hashing must be deterministic and configured off a stable secret per-org. For Private, secret is customer-controlled so we might need a mapping table published during onboarding.
Dana Morris: Add an audit event type `telemetry_policy` whenever a proxy switches sink or redaction mode. That helps security teams.
Maya Bhattacharya: Decision suggestion (short-term): go with unified proxy + mode adapters, implement `handoff.emit` API, canonical exit event, deterministic tenant hashing. Long-term: evaluate splitting binaries if per-mode ops overhead becomes large.
Oliver Chen: +1 for that path. fewer binaries while we iterate. Will need strong feature flags and test harness to simulate private/local sinks.
Samir Patel: I'll draft the adapter interface PR: `Adapter.handoffEmit(map[string]interface{})` and a mock `localSink` for e2e tests.
Jen Li: I'll write telemetry schema doc and list required redaction fields + sampling guidance.
Maya Bhattacharya: Action items: Samir (adapter PR, due EoW), Jen (telemetry schema + compliance checklist, due Wed), Oliver (run canary with sample rate 1% on staging), Dana (confirm audit event content).
Infra-bot: Deploy pipeline note — remember to include canary tag `proxy-unified-canary` when Oliver runs canary.
Maya Bhattacharya: Thanks all, if no objections I'll merge this plan into the hosting-abstraction RFC as a follow-up. :thumbsup:
Oliver Chen: No objections from infra.
Jen Li: Fine with me, will sync if privacy legal flags anything.
Samir Patel: Sounds good, starting the PR now.
Dana Morris: 👍
Maya Bhattacharya: Closing thread — will add follow-up checklist to the RFC doc.
